behaviours.description: Compares each string's maximum and minimum cell voltage against three nested over- and under-voltage tiers and raises the matching diagnosis entry on each tier, clearing the tiers the value has returned inside.
Raises an additional deep-discharge diagnosis when the undervoltage-MSL handler reports an error and the minimum voltage is also at or below the deep-discharge threshold.
Selects between the discharge and the charge temperature tier sets from the sign of the string current.
Skips a string's current comparison entirely when the database marks that string current invalid, so an untrusted measurement does not raise a limit diagnosis.
Compares absolute string current against direction-specific string and cell current limits and against the pack current limit.
The diagnosis handler every SOA check calls into; the per-entry occurrence threshold and delay in the configuration table decide whether a raised entry becomes active.

The configuration rows that grade the three voltage tiers, where only the MSL tier is configured as a fatal error and the outer two discard their delay - the reason an outer-band excursion is recorded without a contactor opening.

concurrency_and_isr_context.shared_state: None in this module at the pinned commit: the functions hold no static state and write only through DIAG_Handler and the caller-supplied structures. The call site is BMS_Trigger (bms.c:898-1691), which invokes them in sequence at bms.c:913-916 before the application's own re-entrance guard. The proposed debounce counter would be the first static state this module would carry, and would introduce a per-cell write from that call site.

limitations: The proposed_location entry names a symbol that DOES NOT EXIST in the pinned source and is not a source anchor. It is a proposal for the hypothetical project and is recorded here precisely so that it cannot be mistaken for a verified location or for an implemented debounce.

The absence of any debounce in soa.c was established by reading the file in full at the pinned commit and searching it for counter, debounce and consecutive, which return no occurrence. It is an absence claim and is stated as such; it is not a claim that no debounce exists anywhere in the product, and the DIAG layer's occurrence counter is named explicitly as the mechanism that does exist.
Behaviour was verified by reading the code. Nothing was executed and no timing or latency measurement of this module exists in this corpus.
soa.c, diag.c and diag_cfg.c are unmodified between the pin and the working tree, so the same ranges and hashes hold for the checked-out files.
evidence_status.method: Every code_location was read at the pinned commit with 'git show 308028fb:path'; each content_hash is that pinned blob's sha256. For the three soa.c locations and the diag.c location, the hash equals the value the corresponding pre-existing source-registry anchor already carries. Each named symbol was confirmed to occur inside its recorded line_range at the pin and each range was confirmed within the file. The three soa.c spans were cross-read against 'graft skeleton src/app/application/soa/soa.c'.

guard.statement: This record describes the hypothetical reference project's SOA implementation against the real pinned source and declares, as a proposal, the debounce counter its design requires and the source does not contain. It is not evidence that FB2-SW-SWR-000002 is met in either profile: the requirement's 10 ms comparison latency and its debounce behaviour are not established by anything listed here, and the debounce is explicitly declared absent. It confers no production authority, no verification credit and no human approval, and it asserts nothing about the real foxBMS product's safety classification.

partial_coverage: The design's DEBOUNCING state, its 'Debounce count configurable (default 2)' constraint and its per-cell debounce decision are not realised in the pinned source and are declared in proposed_location as not_in_source.

The design's VIOLATION_CONFIRMED -> FAULT_TRIGGERED path and its 'fault_request' output are not an output of the comparison module, which returns void. In the source the fault request is raised downstream by BMS_IsAnyFatalErrorFlagSet and BMS_IsBatterySystemStateOkay polling the DIAG fatal-error link table, so the reference project's declared interface is realised by a mechanism the design does not describe.
The design's 'violation_details' output does not exist in the source; the detail carried out of the comparison is the DIAG occurrence counter.

The design's implementation_mapping asserts SOA_CheckVoltageLimits, SOA_CheckCurrentLimits, SOA_CheckTemperatureLimits and DIAG_CBS_Voltage; none of those four names occurs anywhere in the repository. That mapping is not repaired here and the disagreement is recorded rather than propagated.

SOA_CheckSlaveTemperatures (soa.c:353-354) is an empty body carrying only a TODO at the pinned commit. It is named here so the record does not imply slave-temperature supervision is implemented in the reference project by this code.
The design's 'Check latency < 10 ms' and 'Stack usage: < 1 KB' constraints are not established by anything in this record; neither figure is measured anywhere in this corpus for this module.
implements.relationship: This is where the reference project's FB2-SW-DSN-000002 limit-comparison and diagnosis-raising responsibilities are realised. The mechanism is the real one, read from the pinned source and verified there: SOA_CheckVoltages (soa.c:81-146) iterates the strings and compares each string's maximum and minimum cell voltage against the nested MOL, RSL and MSL thresholds, raising DIAG_HANDLER for each tier crossed and clearing the tiers the value has returned inside, and additionally raises the deep-discharge entry when the undervoltage-MSL handler reports an error and the minimum is at or below the deep-discharge threshold; SOA_CheckTemperatures (148-269) selects the discharge or the charge tier set from the sign of the string current; SOA_CheckCurrent (271-351) skips a string whose current the database marks invalid and otherwise compares absolute current against direction-specific limits and raises the current-on-open-string entry. The severity and delay each raised entry actually carries come from the DIAG configuration table (diag_cfg.c:126-131), where the MSL tier is the only one configured DIAG_FATAL_ERROR and the RSL and MOL tiers are DIAG_WARNING and DIAG_INFO with DIAG_DELAY_DISCARD - so an excursion into the outer bands is recorded and produces no contactor opening. The reference project reuses this comparison and adds the debounce the design requires and the source lacks, declared in proposed_location.

proposed_location.why_not_in_source: The reference project's design FB2-SW-DSN-000002 requires a debounce of a configurable number of consecutive violations before a violation is classified, sets the default count at 2 in its own constraints, and selects per-cell debounce in decision DEC-SOA-002. The pinned soa.c contains no counter, no static state and no debounce of any kind: a search of the file for counter, debounce and consecutive at the pinned commit returns nothing. What the source does instead is configure a per-diagnosis-entry occurrence threshold and delay in the DIAG layer (diag_cfg.c:126-131 gives the cell-voltage tiers DIAG_SEN_EVENT_50, with DIAG_DELAY_200ms on the MSL tier and DIAG_DELAY_DISCARD on RSL and MOL), which is a different mechanism at a different layer, with different parameters and a different granularity from the design's per-cell debounce. The proposed symbol is therefore a new element the reference project would have to add; it does not exist in the product and is not presented as if it did.

record_verbatim.provenance_note: This record shares its anchor set with the as_is record of the same id, because both profiles describe the same real source. No new anchor was created. The not_in_source proposal is grounded in a contradiction the corpus had already recorded rather than in a fresh inference: the fault_reaction field of FB2-SAF-FSR-000002 in the as_is profile states that the source implements no counter in the SOA module and configures the MSL tier at 50 events with a 200 ms delay, and that no 5 ms classification figure exists in the configuration.

realises_requirements.how_realised: The limit comparison the requirement describes is present and reused. The debounce the requirement's acceptance criteria depend on is not in the source and is declared as a proposal, so the reference project's realisation of this requirement is incomplete at revision 1 and would need the proposed counter to satisfy its debounce criterion.

revision_history.description: First issue. The reference project's design FB2-SW-DSN-000002 requires a per-cell debounce with a configurable count and its decision DEC-SOA-002 selects per-cell debounce explicitly. The pinned source implements no counter in the SOA module at all - a fact this corpus already records in the fault-reaction fields of FB2-SAF-FSR-000002 in the as_is profile. That gap is declared here as an explicit not_in_source proposal rather than being papered over by presenting the DIAG occurrence counter as the design's debounce.

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/<profile>/<id>.json, then record the approval as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block on the record, plus approval_ledger_ref naming one appended line in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. Do NOT add a revision_history entry: see docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md.

As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract. Since the same day (amendment APPROVAL-LEDGER-A1) the approval is recorded in the append-only ledger at docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl and the record keeps only a reference to it, so recording your signature neither bumps the revision nor invalidates any review digest.
